title: Naciketas reached Brahman
theme: Having received from Death this knowledge and the whole rule of yoga, Naciketas reached Brahman, free of passion and of death; so does any other who knows thus the inner self.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., written as an a-stem (naciketa-)
words.context: Śaṅkara glosses with the regular nominative, «नचिकेताः»
Raṅgarāmānuja: what was taught from ‘yadā pañca’, «इत्यादिना उक्तं योगविधिं च»

sandhi.type: m before a consonant; aḥ before a
sandhi.rule: Final m → anusvāra before a consonant, P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः). The visarga of -aḥ becomes u before a, giving o, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च) with P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः), and the following a is merged, P. 6.1.109 (एङः पदान्तादति); the avagraha marks it.

sandhi.type: m before a vowel; m before a consonant
sandhi.rule: Final m stays before a vowel and is joined to it. Final m → anusvāra before a consonant, P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः).

sandhi.type: aḥ before a voiced consonant; aḥ before a; t before a voiced sound; uḥ before a vowel; i before an unlike vowel
sandhi.rule: -aḥ becomes -o before a voiced consonant, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च). The visarga of -aḥ becomes u before a, giving o, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च) with P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः), and the following a is merged, P. 6.1.109 (एङः पदान्तादति); the avagraha marks it. A final t becomes d before a voiced sound, P. 8.2.39 (झलां जशोऽन्ते). After i or u the visarga becomes r before a voiced sound: the s becomes ru, P. 8.2.66 (ससजुषो रुँः). i before an unlike vowel becomes y, P. 6.1.77 (इको यणचि).

sandhi.type: aḥ before a voiced consonant; t before a vowel; m before a vowel
sandhi.rule: -aḥ becomes -o before a voiced consonant, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च). A final t becomes d before a voiced sound, P. 8.2.39 (झलां जशोऽन्ते). Final m stays before a vowel and is joined to it.

samasa.meaning: the rule, the method of yoga

morphology.note: The name is an s-stem, Naciketas, whose nominative is naciketāḥ (1.1.1). Here the text has naciketo ’tha, which presupposes naciketaḥ, a nominative inflected as if from an a-stem. Śaṅkara glosses with the regular form, «नचिकेताः»; Madhva’s text reads nāciketaḥ (corrections.json).

A root noun from √vid, ‘knower’, in the nominative; with yaḥ: ‘who [is] a knower’. Śaṅkara takes evaṃ with it, ‘one who knows thus’, «एवंवित्»; Raṅgarāmānuja paraphrases ‘who knows the knowledge of the inner self’.
Written as an a-stem nominative (viraja-, ‘free of rajas’); Śaṅkara glosses with the s-stem form virajāḥ, «विगतरजाः».

translation.literal: Having then received this knowledge taught by Death, and the whole rule of yoga, Naciketas became one who has reached Brahman, free of passion, free of death; another too who [is] thus a knower of the inner self itself.
translation.readable: Naciketas received from Death this knowledge and the whole discipline of yoga, and reached Brahman, free of all stain and of death. So will any other who knows the inner self in this way.

syntax: The absolutive clause mṛtyuproktāṃ … labdhvā (with two objects, vidyām etām and yogavidhiṃ kṛtsnam) leads to the main clause brahma prāpto virajo ’bhūd vimṛtyuḥ, with Naciketas as subject. The closing clause anyo ’py evaṃ yo vid adhyātmam eva has no verb of its own: ‘[becomes so]’ is supplied from the main clause, as Śaṅkara supplies it.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: he became free, released, «मुक्तोऽभवदित्यर्थः», free of merit and demerit and of desire and ignorance. Raṅgarāmānuja: reaching Brahman as the Chāndogya describes (quoted by him), «परं ज्योतिरुपसम्पद्य स्वेन रूपेणाभिनिष्पद्यते», he became one in whom the eight qualities are manifest, «आविर्भूतगुणाष्टकोऽभूत् इत्यर्थः».
Śaṅkara: the inner self as it truly is, not by courtesy, «अध्यात्ममेव निरुपचरितं प्रत्यक्स्वरूपं». Raṅgarāmānuja: the knowledge of the inner self, «अध्यात्ममेव अध्यात्मविद्यां य: अन्योऽपि वेत्ति».

metre.name: triṣṭubh
metre.note: Regular: 22 and 22 syllables (11 + 11 in each line).

beginner: The Upaniṣad ends by returning to its story. Naciketas, the boy who went to Death and refused every distraction, received this knowledge and the whole discipline of yoga, and reached Brahman, free of stain and free of death. Then the promise widens: anyone else who knows the inner self in this way will reach the same. Śaṅkara says the story is told to praise the knowledge: Naciketas became free, rid of merit and demerit, desire and ignorance, and so can anyone. Raṅgarāmānuja says Naciketas reached Brahman and his true nature shone out with its eight qualities, as the Chāndogya describes, and that ‘the whole rule of yoga’ is the discipline taught from ‘when the five senses rest’. Madhva’s bhāṣya ends here with its own closing words: that Viṣṇu is supreme.
analogy: A teacher closes the lesson by pointing to the student who first learned it, and says: you can stand where he stands.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: Having received from Death this knowledge and the whole rule of yoga, Naciketas reached Brahman, free of stain and of death; so too any other who thus knows the inner self.

commentary.q: Śaṅkara: the story told in praise of the knowledge
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The story’s conclusion is told to praise the knowledge, «विद्यास्तुत्यर्थोऽयमाख्यायिकार्थोपसंहारः». Naciketas received the knowledge and the whole yoga, with its aids and fruit, «समस्तं सोपकरणं सफलमित्येतत्», and reached Brahman, that is, became free, «मुक्तोऽभवदित्यर्थः», free of merit and demerit, «विगतधर्माधर्मः», and of desire and ignorance. Not he alone: anyone who knows the inner self as it truly is, «अध्यात्ममेव निरुपचरितं प्रत्यक्स्वरूपं», becomes free of death.

commentary.q: Raṅgarāmānuja: reaching Brahman, the true nature shining forth
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: He concludes the story: Naciketas received the knowledge of the self and the rule of yoga taught from ‘yadā pañca’, «इत्यादिना उक्तं योगविधिं च», and reached Brahman as the Chāndogya describes, «परं ज्योतिरुपसम्पद्य स्वेन रूपेणाभिनिष्पद्यते», becoming one in whom the eight qualities are manifest, «आविर्भूतगुणाष्टकोऽभूत् इत्यर्थः». Anyone else who knows the knowledge of the inner self becomes like Naciketas.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Madhva’s bhāṣya has no comment of its own on this mantra. After the colophon of the Upaniṣad it closes with its own conclusion, «अतः सर्वोत्तमो विष्णुरिति सिद्धम्», and a verse of homage. Śaṅkara’s and Raṅgarāmānuja’s entries end with the closing śānti, which this edition keeps apart from the numbered text.

commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: The Chāndogya describes the self in the same words: «य आत्मापहतपाप्मा विजरो विमृत्युर्विशोको».

advaita.text: To reach Brahman is to be released, «मुक्तोऽभवदित्यर्थः»; the same awaits anyone who knows the inner self as it truly is.

visistadvaita.text: Reaching Brahman, the self’s own nature with its eight qualities becomes manifest, «आविर्भूतगुणाष्टकोऽभूत् इत्यर्थः».

schools.disagreement: Both read the verse as the fruit of the knowledge. For Śaṅkara, reaching Brahman is release, freedom from merit, demerit, desire and ignorance; for Raṅgarāmānuja it is the soul reaching Brahman and its own nature, with its eight qualities, becoming manifest. Madhva’s bhāṣya has no comment of its own on this mantra; it closes by stating that Viṣṇu is supreme.

parallels.note: Quoted by Raṅgarāmānuja: reaching the highest light, the self appears in its own form.
The self free of evil, old age and death in the Chāndogya.

parallels.quote: अध्यात्मयोगाधिगमेन देवं मत्वा धीरो हर्षशोकौ जहाति
parallels.note: The Kaṭha’s inward yoga, now given in full.

contemporary.text: The Kaṭha began with a boy who would not be put off, and ends by saying that what he learned is open to anyone who learns it the same way. Few teachings end by handing the student’s place to the reader. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: What did Naciketas do that made him able to receive this teaching?
reflect.deeper: Is ‘reaching Brahman’ becoming free, or becoming fully oneself? What does each reading make of the last line’s promise?
reflect.practice: Reread the first verse of the Kaṭha and this last one together.

references.text: Raṅgarāmānuja’s entry on this mantra continues, after his comment, with the closing śānti and his gloss on it, a summary of the three Brahmasūtra adhikaraṇas he says decide that the whole Upaniṣad concerns the Lord, a verse of homage to Rāmānuja, and his colophon; Śaṅkara’s entry ends with the śānti. None of this is quoted as comment on the verse.

flags.note: Madhva’s text reads nāciketaḥ for naciketaḥ (corrections.json).

naciketaḥ and virajaḥ are written as a-stem nominatives of the s-stems naciketas and virajas; Śaṅkara glosses with the regular nominatives (naciketāḥ, virajāḥ). The edition keeps the form the witnesses print.
Reaching Brahman as release (Śaṅkara) or as reaching Brahman with one’s own nature manifest (Raṅgarāmānuja).
madhva.json under 2.3.18 holds only the bhāṣya’s closing colophon, its concluding sentence and a verse of homage; Madhva has no comment on the verse itself, and no dvaita position is given.
